why: B (Example 1): for every abstract connected Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with a Levi-Civita connection whose curvature vanishes identically (flat) and every geodesic γ on [0,1]: Jacobi ⇔ D²J/dt² = 0, a non-zero Jacobi field has at most one zero in [0,1], no conjugate parameters, nullity of E_** = 0. A (universes 0): only for slice submanifolds of CODIMENSION 0 (every tangent space = V, i.e. open subsets of V): open sets are slice submanifolds; curvature = 0; along any curve in N on (0,1) (not only geodesics) Jacobi fields are affine and there are no conjugate points; hessNullity = 0 along geodesics. A ⇒ B fails genuinely, even on embedded manifolds: A only treats codimension-0 submanifolds, while flat manifolds include e.g. flat cylinders/tori and every 1-manifold, which are not open subsets of their ambient space (and the abstract setting). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: A's 'codimension 0 ⇒ flat' and its statements along arbitrary (non-geodesic) curves are not in B. Restricted to codimension-0 embedded manifolds, A ⇒ B's clauses (1)–(3) and B ⇒ A's 'no conjugate points' along geodesics are proved.
